channel.title: The Fox News Rundown
channel.description: The FOX News Rundown is your daily news podcast for making sense of the big issues directly impacting your life. Go beyond the headlines every morning and join some of FOX News’ most exceptional journalists—including FOX News Channel reporters Peter Doocy, Aishah Hasnie, Bill Melugin, Alex Hogan, Lucas Tomlinson and Jacqui Heinrich and FOX News Radio reporters Dave Anthony, Jessica Rosenthal, Lisa Brady, and Gurnal Scott - as they tap into the global reporting resources of FOX News and get unparalleled political analysis and exclusive insight from top newsmakers. The Rundown offers a sharp contrast of perspectives you won’t hear anywhere else, and a daily commentary you can't miss, we deliver the full picture of the day's biggest events.

item.title: Karl Rove On How Republicans Can Right The Ship
item.description:
Election results indicate Democrats have dealt Republicans sweeping defeats across the country, flipping key seats in traditional red bastions and securing majorities in both the House and Senate. FOX News Contributor and former Deputy Chief of Staff to President George W. Bush Karl Rove examines how President Trump’s endorsements influenced critical races, what challenges the incoming Speaker of the House faces to deliver on Democratic promises, and what this pivotal defeat means for the 2028 presidential cycle.
Following a difficult midterm election for Republicans, questions are mounting over how foreign policy—particularly the ongoing conflict with Iran—impacted voters at the ballot box. Victoria Coates, Vice President of the Institute for National Security at the Heritage Foundation, joins FOX News correspondent Lucas Tomlinson to analyze President Trump's and Vice President JD Vance's post-election remarks on the war and the financial pressure mounting on Tehran under Operation Economic Outcast.
PLUS, commentary by Rich Zeoli, host of The Rich Zeoli Podcast.

item.title: How Florida Avoided the Blue Wave
item.description:
Florida elected its first Black Republican governor, Byron Donalds, who is taking the helm after eight years under Ron DeSantis. Sen. Ashley Moody also held her seat against Democratic Socialist Angie Nixon, who faced scrutiny for hedging on whether Cuba is a dictatorship, her DSA membership and using a megaphone to disrupt a vote on new congressional maps. How did the Sunshine State avoid the 'blue wave'?
FOX's Eben Brown speaks to Francis Suarez, former Mayor of Miami, who says the difference was in quality of Republican candidate in Florida.

item.title: The New Political Landscape: House and Senate Shift Left In Blue Wave
item.description:
Democrats have seized both the House and Senate majorities in a historic blue wave, pulling off big wins in battleground districts and flipping traditionally red, safe seats. FOX News Audio Washington, D.C., Political Anchor and Correspondent Jared Halpern sits down with FOX News Radio Reporter Jessica Rosenthal to discuss all the results from election night.
After the Democrats' big wins Tuesday, what’s next for both parties? And what lessons should they take away? Republican Strategist and Co-Founder of South & Hill Strategies Colin Reed joins the Rundown to break down what the election results mean for the direction of the country, as well as the remainder of President Trump's term and the 2028 presidential election.
PLUS, commentary by Jimmy Failla, host of FOX News Saturday Night and FOX News Radio’s FOX Across America.

item.title: Election Day: Martha MacCallum on Expectations, Stakes, and Potential Surprises
item.description:
As Americans head to the voting booth, Capitol Hill’s balance of power may hinge on whether high grocery bills and foreign conflicts outweigh standard economic indicators. Host of The Untold Story podcast and anchor of The Story on FOX News, Martha MacCallum explains why polling models might be missing key trends, how young men and Hispanic voters are reacting to the war in Iran and housing costs, and the closely watched Michigan race testing the reach of Democratic socialism.
Election day is here and control of Congress is now up to the voters. After months of campaigning, Washington D.C. will either see Republicans hold onto their slim majorities or Democrats capture enough seats to win the majority in either or both chambers. Tom Bevan, Co-Founder and Executive Editor of RealClearPolitics, joins FOX's Lucas Tomlinson to break down what to expect as results begin rolling in. Bevan analyzes the battleground map and why polling is predicting good outcomes for Democrats.
PLUS, commentary by Brian Kilmeade, Host of “The Brian Kilmeade Show”, Co-Host of FOX & Friends and Host of One Nation with Brian Kilmeade Learn more about your ad choices. Visit podcastchoices.com/adchoices

item.title: Midterms 2026: The Tightest and Most Contentious Races to Follow
item.description:
Just hours to go before polls open for the midterm elections and we will take you around the country where critical contests will decide control of Congress.435 seats in the U-S House and 35 Senate seats will be decided this week in the midterm elections. Control of both chambers will likely rest with just a handful of contests with the final FOX News power rankings giving Democrats an advantage to flip the house, with just 17 toss ups, but the Senate is very much in play with 7 toss up races in some deep red states likely to tip the balance.
FOX's Jared Halpern speaks with FOX News Radio's team of reporters around the country covering the tightest and most contentious races - FOX's Jeff Monosso is in Michigan, Krystin Goodwin is in Texas, Tonya J. Powers is in Maine, and Eben Brown is in Florida.
